stormwell-evidence-lock.name: Stormwell Archive — Evidence Lock
stormwell-evidence-lock.text: A compact sealed intake bay just inside a field airlock: matte white and dark-blue surfaces, floor markings, fixed cameras, isolation cabinets, contamination hood, evidence tables, tamper-seal printer, and no ceremonial decoration. Objects enter here before they enter the ship's analytic network.

stormwell-forensic-lab.name: Stormwell Archive — Forensic Reconstruction Lab
stormwell-forensic-lab.text: A working archival-science laboratory built into a converted carrier bay: modular benches, microscopes, physical-media fixtures, shielded test racks, cable looms, removable clean enclosures, spare processors, reference instruments, and rolling carts of obsolete hardware. Modern Fleet systems coexist with preserved legacy machines because old records often require old assumptions to be reconstructed.

stormwell-analysis-gallery.name: Stormwell Archive — Analysis Gallery
stormwell-analysis-gallery.text: A long quiet operations room with wall-sized evidence timelines, provenance graphs, synchronized telemetry plots, version trees, and confidence annotations. The room is arranged for teams to compare sources side by side, not for spectacle; visual information is sparse, legible, and functional.

stormwell-bridge.name: Stormwell Archive — Bridge
stormwell-bridge.text: A mature Fleet bridge in blue-white materials with restrained gold structure, broad forward display, navigation stations, evidence liaison console, and an unusually large side workspace for briefing uncertain findings to command. It is operational, not ceremonial.

stormwell-hardware-vault.name: Stormwell Archive — Hardware Reference Vault
stormwell-hardware-vault.text: Dense but orderly storage aisles containing preserved obsolete processors, sensor interface boards, removable media readers, clock modules, calibration standards, and tagged reference instruments. It resembles a technical standards laboratory crossed with a machine archive, not a museum.

far-lantern-wreck.name: Far Lantern Wreck Site
far-lantern-wreck.text: A broken civilian corridor-survey cutter suspended near a dim Lattice margin: hull split along the midships frame, sensor booms twisted, one recorder capsule embedded in a detached equipment spine, salvage lights cutting through drifting ice and metal fragments. No bodies are shown.

lattice-harrow-fold.name: Harrow Fold — Lattice Margin
lattice-harrow-fold.text: A navigable but unstable corridor margin where distant stars shear slightly out of alignment and thin blue-white gravitic interference bands appear only on instruments and at the edge of vision. It should feel physically strange but not mystical.

civil-survey-office.name: Civil Survey Service — Remote Cartography Office
civil-survey-office.text: A practical civilian mapping office on a Verge station with layered route displays, survey trace archives, battered field equipment, and staff working at ordinary desks. Materials are functional and underfunded compared with Fleet spaces.
